headline: Campground Reservations and Entry Fee Details
reservation: Joshua Tree National Park requires a park pass for entry, which can be purchased at stations or online. Most campgrounds require reservations through Recreation.gov months in advance during the October–May peak season; first-come, first-served sites are extremely limited and typically fill by Thursday for the weekend.

days.title: Boulders and High Desert Overlooks
days.start: Suggested: 8 AM from Joshua Tree Village

stops.name: Hidden Valley Loop
stops.detail: Walk the one-mile trail enclosed by massive rock walls to see a variety of desert plants and monzogranite formations.

stops.name: Keys View
stops.detail: Drive to the crest of the Little San Bernardino Mountains for a view of the San Andreas Fault and Coachella Valley.

days.driving: Allow 1.5 hours for park transit; roads are paved but speed limits are low
days.note: Hidden Valley parking is often at capacity by 10 AM; have a backup stop like Quail Springs ready.

days.title: Historical Water and Desert Peaks

stops.name: Barker Dam
stops.detail: Observe the seasonal water tank and petroglyphs on a 1.1-mile loop; water levels depend entirely on recent rainfall.

stops.name: Ryan Mountain
stops.detail: Climb 1,000 feet for a central view of the park's rock piles; this trail offers no shade and requires significant water.

days.driving: Allow 1 hour total travel; focus on the Park Boulevard corridor
days.note: Do not attempt Ryan Mountain if temperatures exceed 90°F (32°C); there is high risk of heat exhaustion.

days.title: The Transition Zone and Cholla Gardens

stops.name: Cholla Cactus Garden
stops.detail: Walk the boardwalk through a dense stand of 'jumping' cholla; stay on the path to avoid painful spines.

stops.name: Arch Rock
stops.detail: A short hike from the Twin Tanks or White Tank area to view a natural granite span and surrounding boulders.

days.driving: Allow 2 hours; the drive to the southern Cottonwood area is longer than the northern loops
days.note: Bee activity can be high near moisture sources and certain flowering plants; use caution if allergic.

intel.title: Trailhead Congestion
intel.text: Parking at popular spots like Skull Rock and Barker Dam is extremely limited. If a lot is full, move to the next destination rather than parking on fragile desert vegetation.

intel.title: No In-Park Connectivity
intel.text: Cell service ends shortly after passing the entrance stations. Do not rely on GPS apps that require a live data connection for navigation.

intel.title: Gateway Supply Only
intel.text: No gasoline, food, or water is available within the park. Refill all supplies in Yucca Valley or Twentynine Palms before entering.

intel.title: Stargazing and Dark Skies
intel.text: The park is an International Dark Sky Park; parking lots remain open for stargazing. Use red-filtered flashlights to preserve your night vision and that of others.

intel.title: Entrance Station Queues
intel.text: The West Entrance (Joshua Tree) can have wait times exceeding one hour on spring weekends. Consider using the North Entrance in Twentynine Palms for faster access.

plan.arrival: Fly into Palm Springs (PSP), rent a vehicle, and purchase at least one gallon of water per person per day at a grocery store in Yucca Valley.
plan.vehicle: Standard vehicles are fine for paved roads; check rental contracts before driving on unpaved routes like Geology Tour Road.
plan.goldenHour: Keys View for sunset, looking across the Coachella Valley toward Mount San Jacinto.
